conventions.convention: Spatial velocities are almost-everywhere classes in H=L²(D,λ;Rᵈ), with 0<λ(D)<∞. The sensor is the integral pairing against ψ∈H, not point evaluation.

The general state interface supplies a separable real Banach space and strong measurability via simple approximants outside a measurable null set. Scalar evaluations use measurable versions; completeness of the probability measure is not assumed.
The matrix norm is Frobenius, (a⊗b)ij=ai bj, and A:B=Σij Aij Bij. Countable Choice is explicitly assumed for the L¹ and L² completeness used in Bochner integration.

R is the covariance tensor E[(U−ū)⊗(U−ū)], without a density factor or a negative stress sign. Pointwise covariance requires the stipulated product-measurable representative. Weak testing uses essentially bounded tensor fields.

The time-dependent Reynolds equation is conditional on the displayed pathwise distributional identities and moment bounds. The gradient convention is (∇φ)ij=∂jφi; pressure is per unit constant density. No existence, boundary trace, initial trace, or closure is asserted.

CLT sums start at k=0 and end at n−1. Their variance is the absolutely convergent covariance sum, including variance zero. Total variation is the event supremum. AC is explicit; stationarity and mixing are hypotheses, not consequences of fluid dynamics.
N(m,v) uses variance v. The AR(1) model assumes |ρ|<1, η>0, stationary joint Gaussianity, and independent N(0,η²) innovations independent of X₀.

load_bearing.statement: A finite-second-moment random velocity law is a probability measure μ on the norm-Borel space H=L²(D,λ;Rᵈ), with 0<λ(D)<∞ and ∫H‖v‖H² dμ(v)<∞. For ψ∈H, Sψ(v)=∫D v·ψ dλ and fψ(v)=Sψ(v)−∫H Sψ dμ. The separate general interface supplies a separable real Banach state space and strongly measurable states with finite second moment.

For the spatial law in the Definition and every ψ∈H, Sψ is finite, representative-independent, linear and continuous, with |Sψ(v)|≤‖v‖H‖ψ‖H; its centered observable is Borel and in L²(μ). For the supplied general Banach interface, the Bochner mean exists, bounded linear sensor expectations commute with that mean, and the finite sensor covariance matrix is well-defined and positive semidefinite.

Assume Countable Choice. For H as in the Definition and K=L¹(D,λ;Rᵈˣᵈ) with Frobenius norm, v⊗w is representative-independent and ‖v⊗w‖K≤‖v‖H‖w‖H. A strongly measurable U with E‖U‖H²<∞ has Bochner-integrable U and U⊗U, with E‖U⊗U‖K=E‖U‖H².

Under Countable Choice, strong measurability, finite second moment and the supplied product-measurable representative, the mean and covariance satisfy E∫D(U⊗U):Φ dλ=∫D(ū⊗ū+R):Φ dλ for every essentially bounded measurable tensor test Φ, with R∈L¹ symmetric positive semidefinite almost everywhere. Under the additional displayed jointly measurable space-time fields, moment bounds and pathwise weak incompressible equation, expectation gives the displayed weak equation with convection tensor m⊗m+R; the stated local version also holds.

Assume AC. The general centered strictly stationary square-integrable observable satisfies the covariance-sum CLT under any of the three stated strong-mixing/moment regimes. The stationary Markov sensor branch satisfies that CLT under the stated countably generated, invariant, path-shift-ergodic, irreducible, aperiodic Harris hypotheses and any of the six displayed rate/moment regimes. Both conclusions include zero variance and absolute covariance summability.
